entry.content:
FINDINGS:
- A multi-agent LLM system splits a problem across several model-driven agents, each with its own role, prompt, tools and memory. [multi_agent_systems.md#0]
- Specialisation lets each agent focus on a narrow job, which tends to improve output quality on tasks that decompose cleanly into research, analysis and writing. [multi_agent_systems.md#0]
- Multi-agent systems carry a real coordination cost. [multi_agent_systems.md#3]
- Every hand-off adds tokens, latency and an opportunity for information to be lost or distorted between agents, so a team of agents can be slower and more expensive than one well-prompted model. [multi_agent_systems.md#3]
- Single-agent systems are simpler to build, debug and evaluate. [multi_agent_systems.md#6]
- A single agent with good tools and retrieval is often the right starting point, and teams should add agents only when specialisation or parallelism clearly pays off on measured evaluations. [multi_agent_systems.md#6]
- Shared memory between agents makes collaboration possible but introduces risk. [memory_for_agents.md#3]
- Without provenance and confidence on each entry, one agent's mistaken note can silently contaminate the work of every other agent. [memory_for_agents.md#3]

# What are the trade-offs between multi-agent and single-agent LLM systems

## Executive summary
A multi-agent LLM system splits a problem across several model-driven agents, each with its own role, prompt, tools and memory. [multi_agent_systems.md#0] Multi-agent systems carry a real coordination cost. [multi_agent_systems.md#3]

## Key findings
- A multi-agent LLM system splits a problem across several model-driven agents, each with its own role, prompt, tools and memory. [multi_agent_systems.md#0]
- Single-agent systems are simpler to build, debug and evaluate. [multi_agent_systems.md#6]
- A single agent with good tools and retrieval is often the right starting point, and teams should add agents only when specialisation or parallelism clearly pays off on measured evaluations. [multi_agent_systems.md#6]
- Specialisation lets each agent focus on a narrow job, which tends to improve output quality on tasks that decompose cleanly into research, analysis and writing. [multi_agent_systems.md#0]
- Without provenance and confidence on each entry, one agent's mistaken note can silently contaminate the work of every other agent. [memory_for_agents.md#3]

## Trade-offs
- Multi-agent systems carry a real coordination cost. [multi_agent_systems.md#3]
- Every hand-off adds tokens, latency and an opportunity for information to be lost or distorted between agents, so a team of agents can be slower and more expensive than one well-prompted model. [multi_agent_systems.md#3]
- Shared memory between agents makes collaboration possible but introduces risk. [memory_for_agents.md#3]

- A multi-agent LLM system splits a problem across several model-driven agents, each with its own role, prompt, tools and memory. [multi_agent_systems.md#0]
